assumptions: A is a linear equivalence because the K-PIK construction and Proposition 3.4 use both A and A^(-1).
The recurrence A(v_j)=v_(j+1) records the paper's two-sided Laurent sequence A^j B.
p48LaurentSpan v m is the paper's Range(V_m)=K_(2m)(A,A^(-m)B), with indices from -m through m-1.

Linear dependence of p48BreakdownDirections v m says that the two new directions A^(-m-1)B and A^m B have rank less than two after quotienting out the old space, exactly the rank-loss premise of Proposition 3.4.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p48_t3_rank_breakdown_invariant (n m : Nat) (hm : 1 <= m) (v : Int -> Fin n -> Real) (A : (Fin n -> Real) ≃ₗ[Real] (Fin n -> Real)) (hstep : forall j, A (v j) = v (j+1)) (hbreak : not (LinearIndependent Real (p48BreakdownDirections v m))) : forall x in p48LaurentSpan v (m+1), A x in p48LaurentSpan v (m+1)
formal_statement.plain_language: If the two new Laurent--Krylov directions at iteration m lose rank after the old space is removed, then the enlarged space is invariant under A.

informal_proof: Extract a nontrivial dependence of the two new quotient directions. If the positive-end coefficient is nonzero, apply A to the relation, solve for the next positive Laurent vector, and close the enlarged span under A. If it is zero, solve for the new negative vector in the old space. Every old generator then has an old preimage under A; injectivity and equality of finite dimensions make A map the old space onto itself. This supplies the missing positive directions and again closes the enlarged span under A.
informal_statement: Prove the invariant-subspace conclusion of Proposition 3.4 from rank loss of the two newly generated K-PIK directions.

tier_rationale: The proof must translate rank loss into a quotient-space dependence, reason separately about the two extreme coefficients, establish old-space invariance in the one-sided case through a finite-dimensional image/finrank argument, obtain the missing boundary Laurent vectors, and close the full enlarged span by induction. This is substantial, comparable to the lower end of validated T2/T3 constructions, and is not discharged by Mathlib imports. The frozen NumStability bundle has no corresponding result, and L uses the same proof as N.
